synopsis: ISO 5006 is described as defining how to measure the machine operator’s field of view from the cab and map blind areas, distinct from ISO 16001’s requirements and tests for detection and visibility aids [f11547, f15204, f15219]. Chapter 7 uses ISO 5006 and ISO 16001 visibility-type methods to illustrate geometric computation of machine coverage and blind zones, with expert opinion supporting this approach [f5602, f5604]. The glossary proposes reproducing these methods, alongside UN R159’s small-cylinder method, in a digital twin of each machine to compute coverage and blind zones before hardware arrives [f11549, f15220]. However, Chapter 3 reports that ISO 5006 was not verified and evidence was not found, a gap repeated in the glossary; the proposed use therefore should not be mistaken for verified application of the standard [f2197, f15219, f15220].
